description: Get details of a specific security configuration scan result. Most controls in a result usually passed; set status to "failed" to get only the controls that need fixing. If the answer is too large, set summary to list the controls without their rules, then set control_id to page through one control's failed paths.

control_id.description: Return one control, for example C-0017, and a page of its paths (what failed and how to fix it) instead of the whole result (optional; not with status, min_severity or summary)

limit.description: With summary: maximum number of controls to return; with control_id: maximum number of paths (optional, default 100, maximum 500)

manifest_name.description: Name of the configuration manifest to get details for (get this from the list_configuration_security_scan_manifests tool)

min_severity.description: Only return controls at or above this severity: Critical, High, Medium or Low (optional)

namespace.description: Namespace of the manifest, as returned by list_configuration_security_scan_manifests (optional, defaults to the namespace in the endpoint's URL)

object_version.description: The object_version of the previous page (optional): if the scan changed since, for example after a rescan, the call fails with OBJECT_CHANGED instead of returning a page of the new version; then start again from offset 0

offset.description: With summary or control_id: number of controls or paths to skip; pass the previous response's next_offset to get the next page (optional, default 0)

status.description: Only return controls with these statuses, comma-separated: failed, passed, skipped (optional; by default every control is returned)

summary.description: Return only each control's ID, name, severity and status, without its rules and paths, a page at a time (optional, default false); works with status and min_severity

name: get_configuration_security_scan_manifest

description: Get details of a specific container profile. A busy container's profile can be large: set section to page through one of its lists (what it executed, opened, called, and its network traffic) instead of getting the whole profile. A profile written by a user can describe several containers: the section answer lists them in containers, and container selects one.

container.description: With section, for a profile that describes several containers: the container to read, by name, or as group/name (containers, initContainers or ephemeralContainers) when a name is in two groups (optional)

limit.description: With section: maximum number of entries to return (optional, default 100, maximum 500)

namespace.description: Namespace of the profile, as returned by list_container_profiles (optional, defaults to the namespace in the endpoint's URL)

object_version.description: The object_version of the previous page (optional): if the profile changed since, for example after a rescan, the call fails with OBJECT_CHANGED instead of returning a page of the new version; then start again from offset 0

offset.description: With section: number of entries to skip; pass the previous response's next_offset to get the next page (optional, default 0)

profile_name.description: Name of the container profile to get details for (get this from the list_container_profiles tool)

section.description: Return only this list of the profile, a page at a time (optional; by default the whole profile is returned)

name: get_container_profile

description: Discover available security configuration scan results at workload level (this returns a list of manifests, not the scan results themselves, to get the scan results, use the get_configuration_security_scan_manifest tool)

continue.description: Optional Kubernetes continuation token for pagination

limit.description: Maximum number of manifests per page (optional, default and maximum 100); lower it if a page is too large, then page with continue

namespace.description: Namespace to list (optional, defaults to the namespace in the endpoint's URL). A workload's scan is stored in the workload's namespace; scans of cluster-scoped resources are in Kubescape's own namespace (usually kubescape)

name: list_configuration_security_scan_manifests

description: Discover available container profiles at workload level (this returns a list of profiles, not the profile results themselves, to get the profile results, use the get_container_profile tool)

continue.description: Optional Kubernetes continuation token for pagination

limit.description: Maximum number of profiles per page (optional, default and maximum 100); lower it if a page is too large, then page with continue

namespace.description: Namespace to list (optional, defaults to the namespace in the endpoint's URL). A container's profile is stored in its workload's namespace

name: list_container_profiles

description: List the packages in an image SBOM (name, version, type, purl, licenses), sorted by name. Returns a page of results (see limit/offset) with the total count. Use name or package_type to look for specific packages.

limit.description: Maximum number of packages to return (optional, default 100, maximum 500)

name.description: Only packages whose name contains this text, case-insensitive (optional)

namespace.description: Namespace of the SBOM (optional, defaults to the namespace in the endpoint's URL)

object_version.description: The object_version of the previous page (optional): if the SBOM changed since, for example after a rescan, the call fails with OBJECT_CHANGED instead of returning a page of the new version; then start again from offset 0

offset.description: Number of packages to skip; pass the previous response's next_offset to get the next page (optional, default 0)

package_type.description: Only packages of this type, for example deb, rpm, apk, npm, python, go-module, java-archive (optional)

sbom_name.description: Name of the SBOM, as returned by list_sboms

name: list_sbom_packages

description: Discover the image SBOMs stored in the cluster, without their content. Use list_sbom_packages to read the packages of one. Kubescape stores them in its own namespace (usually kubescape).

continue.description: Optional Kubernetes continuation token for pagination

limit.description: Maximum number of SBOMs per page (optional, default and maximum 100); lower it if a page is too large, then page with continue

namespace.description: Namespace to list (optional, defaults to the namespace in the endpoint's URL)

name: list_sboms

description: List the vulnerabilities in a given manifest, one entry per CVE and affected package, most severe first. Returns a page of results (see limit/offset) with the total count; long text fields are left out unless include_details is true.

fixable_only.description: Only return vulnerabilities that have a fixed version (optional, default false)

include_details.description: Include description, CVSS, URLs, advisories and data source for each entry, and fix_data_source when the fixed version comes from another source (optional, default false; makes the response much larger)

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (optional, default 100, maximum 500)

manifest_name.description: Name of the manifest to list vulnerabilities from

min_severity.description: Minimum severity to include: Critical, High, Medium, Low, Negligible (optional; by default every severity, including unclassified ones, is returned)

namespace.description: Namespace of the manifest (optional, defaults to the namespace in the endpoint's URL)

object_version.description: The object_version of the previous page (optional): if the manifest changed since, for example after a rescan, the call fails with OBJECT_CHANGED instead of returning a page of the new version; then start again from offset 0

offset.description: Number of entries to skip; pass the previous response's next_offset to get the next page (optional, default 0)

name: list_vulnerabilities_in_manifest

description: Discover available vulnerability manifests at image and workload levels. Kubescape stores them in its own namespace (usually kubescape).

continue.description: Optional Kubernetes continuation token for pagination

level.description: Type of vulnerability manifests to list

limit.description: Maximum number of manifests per page (optional, default and maximum 100); lower it if a page is too large, then page with continue

namespace.description: Namespace to list (optional, defaults to the namespace in the endpoint's URL)

name: list_vulnerability_manifests

description: List the vulnerability matches (full grype records) for a given CVE in a given manifest, one per affected package and vulnerability source. Returns a page of results (see limit/offset) with the total count.

cve_id.description: ID of the CVE to list matches for

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (optional, default 20, maximum 100)

manifest_name.description: Name of the manifest to list vulnerabilities from

namespace.description: Namespace of the manifest (optional, defaults to the namespace in the endpoint's URL)

object_version.description: The object_version of the previous page (optional): if the manifest changed since, for example after a rescan, the call fails with OBJECT_CHANGED instead of returning a page of the new version; then start again from offset 0

offset.description: Number of matches to skip; pass the previous response's next_offset to get the next page (optional, default 0)

name: list_vulnerability_matches_for_cve
